# @andrewhmir/dsh-btw — ephemeral `/btw` side questions for the DSH Web GUI

An **unofficial community plugin** for DeepSeek Harness
(DSH). It adds one gesture to the Web GUI co

official community plugin** for DeepSeek Harness
(DSH). It adds one gesture to the Web GUI composer:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The answer streams into a **non-modal floating card** over the chat — no
backdrop, no focus trap, an

d the composer keeps working while it streams.
Dismissing it leaves **no trace** in the session: the

question and answer are
never appended to the transcript, never rendered as chat rows, and never be

come
part of what the model sees on the next turn.

It is the inverse of a subagent: a subagent gets the full tool surface and an
empty context; `/btw`
gets the full conversation context and no tools.
## What `/btw` does
| property | behavior |
| invocation | `/btw <question>` typed in the composer, mid-session; also selectable from the `/` me

nu |
| context | the full committed conversation of the current session |
| tools | none — the reque

st carries no tool schemas and no tool history |
| answer | streamed into a floating card over the c

hat; thinking progress is shown while it reasons |
| dismissal | the × button, or Escape while the c

ard has focus (Space/Enter are never captured) |
| persistence | none — the exchange never enters se

ssion history |
| concurrency | works while the main turn is streaming and never interrupts it; the

app stays interactive |
| shape | single-shot; no follow-up turns |
| model | the session's routed p

rovider/model/reasoning effort (configurable to `off`) |
| cost | one tool-less call (plus any autom
atic continuation call) whose message prefix is the parent request's prefix, so the provider's promp

t cache is reused |
| completeness | a truncated answer is continued automatically instead of being
shown half-finished |
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` with the Web GUI (`dsh web`).
- Node.js 22 or newer only for the verification

scripts; the plugin itself runs
inside the harness process.

## How it works

- `ui-commands` claims slash commands that exist in the session's **host**
command catalog. `/btw` d

eliberately does not register such a command: a host
command's result is durably logged (`command/ru

n` / `command/done`) and would
enter the session history.
- Instead, the plugin's **client half** re

gisters its own `'/'` input-trigger
source. During composer adjudication it claims `/btw <question>`

before any
host command runs, opens the card, and calls the plugin's own loopback route
`POST /btw/

ask`.
- The **host half** resolves the live agent for the session, snapshots the exact
model-visible

history with `Session.deriveMessages()`, appends one frozen user
message carrying the side question

, and runs a single `ctx.llm.stream()` call
with **no tools, no tool history, and no separate system

prompt**. Because the
message list is the parent request's prefix plus one trailing message, the
pr

ovider's prompt cache is reused.
- The routed wire protocol counts **thinking against the output bud

get**, so the
budget is sized for thinking plus answer (default 8192, capped by the session's
own co

mposed cap). If the budget is exhausted before any visible text exists,
the host retries that round

once with thinking disabled rather than showing an
empty answer.
- A truncated answer is not treated

as final: the host appends the partial text
as an assistant turn plus a "continue exactly where you

stopped" user turn and
keeps streaming (`continuations`, default 2 rounds). Continuation rounds run

without thinking, so the same problem is not reasoned about twice.
- Aborts are progress-based, not

wall-clock: a **stall watchdog** fires when no
chunk at all (thinking included) arrives for `stallT

imeoutMs` (default 60 s),
and a `deadlineMs` ceiling (default 10 min) bounds a wedged request. Both

are
reported as distinct codes so the card can say what happened instead of
silently dropping text.

- The answer streams back as newline-delimited JSON, renders **Markdown** through
the shell's shared

`MarkdownText` component (plain-text fallback if an older
shell does not seed it), and is shown in

a `shell.overlay` card that is
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **In-flight partial assistant text is not included.** The snapshot reads the
committed session sur

face; while the main turn is streaming, the current
assistant message is not committed yet. `/btw` s

ees the conversation as of the
last committed event.
- **Not visible in session-log cost dashboards.

** Ephemeral calls leave no
session-log trace; provider billing is the source of truth for them.
- *

*Web GUI only.** The host route is generic, but the invocation and the card are
client-side Web feat

glish in this version.
- **A future host `btw` command would shadow this plugin.** The host catalog

is
adjudicated before the plugin's source; if a future harness version ships a
host command with the

same name, `/btw` would execute that command instead.
- **Single-shot.** There is no follow-up turn

inside the card; automatic
continuations only finish the same answer.
- **Continuations are bounded

.** After `continuations` rounds a still-truncated
answer is shown with a "still cut off" note rathe

r than continuing forever.
- **The card floats above the chat** (bottom-right). It does not reflow t
pe-while-focused remain available.
## Compatibility

`engines.dsh` declares `>=0.2.0-rc.2`. Both tags were verified on a clean-room
install containing on
ly the official bundles plus this plugin:
| Harness | Result |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` (npm `latest`) | card + streamed answer, uppercase `/BTW`, Markdown, Escape/Space/Ent

er dismissal, warm cache |
| `0.2.1-rc.2` (npm `next`) | the above, plus mid-stream concurrency (4/4
answers during a tool call) and strict ephemerality |

The dismissal contract changed in `0.2.0` (non-modal: × or focused Escape); the
browser suite in `te

st/e2e/` asserts the new contract and must be re-run on a
machine where headless Chrome can launch.

See `docs/VERIFICATION.md`
for what is currently proven and what is pending.
